newsitem.title: EGYPT: Nile waters flow into Toshka overflow canal.
newsitem.headline: Nile waters flow into Toshka overflow canal.

text.p: Nile waters, swollen by torrential rains, gushed into an Egyptian overflow canal on Sunday for the first time since the canal was built in 1978, an Egyptian Aswan Dam official said.

Mina Iskandar, chairman of the Aswan Dam High Authority, said water flowed into the Toshka overflow canal after its level in Lake Nasser, behind the Aswan Dam, reached the record high of 178.10 metres (584 feet) above sea level.
The Nile has risen because because of torrential rains along the Nile in Ethiopia, which caused flooding in Sudan.
The authority says the dam, built in the 1960s under the late Egyptian president Gamal Abdel Nasser, can accomodate a water level of up to 183 metres (600 feet) in Lake Nasser.
But water would be drained into a series of overflow canals, ducts and floodgates before it reached that height
The government has decided to store this year's excess water to irrigate more than 200,000 hectares of desert land.
